title: An Optimization Framework for Differentially Private Sparse Fine-Tuning

problem.claim: The abstract describes a performance gap between differentially private and non-private fine-tuning for private transfer learning.

gap.claim: Existing private sparse fine-tuning often fixes trainable weights or selects them from public-model weights; the authors characterize these choices as suboptimal.

contributions.claim: Proposes an optimization-based approach to sparse fine-tuning neural networks under differential privacy.
The selection method uses private gradient information and off-the-shelf privacy accounting techniques.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present a new approach to sparse fine-tuning under differential privacy.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across multiple vision-model and dataset settings, the authors report higher accuracy for their selector than for full-model private tuning or prior sparse methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Describes DP-SGD as a standard private training and fine-tuning approach and notes the use of pretrained checkpoints.
States a performance gap between DP-SGD fine-tuning and non-private counterparts.
Notes sparse fine-tuning and identifies fixed or public-weight-based selection as existing approaches the authors regard as suboptimal.
Uses optimization-based weight selection with private gradient information and standard privacy accounting.
Reports prediction-accuracy comparisons on several computer-vision models and datasets.

source_observation.claim: The selection method uses private gradient information, and experiments compare it with full-model private fine-tuning and existing sparse approaches.

interpretation.claim: The paper motivates data-dependent weight selection under privacy constraints rather than fixed or public-weight-based selection.

application.claim: For private fine-tuning, compare private-gradient-based selection with fixed-subset and full-model alternatives.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported advantage generalizes beyond the stated computer-vision models and datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify privacy parameters or accounting configuration.
It does not identify models, datasets, baselines, or quantitative accuracy gains.
It does not describe the optimization procedure or computational overhead.
